cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is a prisoner on his way to Rome. His ship wrecked, but everyone on board made it safely to land on the island of Malta (Acts 27:44; 28:1). Now it's time to get back on the water.

cards.question: How long do Paul and the others stay on Malta before they set sail again?

cards.text: They board an Alexandrian ship that spent the winter at the island, with the Twin Brothers as its figurehead. After one shipwreck, friend, I'm checking that boat for leaks BEFORE I sit down.
Three days at Syracuse, a stop at Rhegium, then a south wind comes up, and they reach Puteoli. That's more stops than my morning commute, and I LIVE in my bakery.

cards.question: When Paul and the others land in Puteoli, who do they find there?
The brothers in Puteoli invite Paul's group to stay with them. For how long?

cards.text: And so they come to Rome, and believers there who heard about them travel as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet them. When my drawer opened, people were looking for tape, not me.

cards.question: When Paul sees the believers from Rome who came out to meet him, what does he do?

answers.text: He is encouraged and thanks God
He tells them to go back home
He worries they will be arrested

cards.text: They make it into Rome. Paul's still a prisoner, but where he ends up might surprise you.

cards.question: Where does the prisoner Paul get to stay in Rome?

answers.text: By himself with a soldier to guard him
In the city prison with other prisoners
In the house of a Roman official

cards.text: After three days, Paul calls together the leaders of the Jews in Rome. Once they've gathered, he speaks to them as brothers.

cards.question: Paul admits to the leaders that he has done something against their people and the customs of their fathers.

cards.text: Even so, Paul says, he was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans. They examined him and found no basis for a death sentence.

cards.question: After examining Paul, what did the Romans want to do with him?

answers.text: Keep him in chains for life

cards.text: But when the Jews objected, Paul was compelled to appeal to Caesar. That's like your manager saying you're good to go, then somebody complains, and now you're on a flight to corporate HEADQUARTERS.

cards.question: Paul tells the leaders he came to Rome to bring a charge against his own nation.
Paul tells the leaders why he is bound with this chain. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Because of the hope of Israel
Because he broke a Roman law

cards.text: The leaders say no letters about Paul came from Judea, and nobody from there said anything bad about him. I bet Paul walked in braced for drama, and the group chat was DEAD quiet.

cards.question: So what do the Jewish leaders in Rome want from Paul?
The leaders tell Paul that this sect is welcomed by people everywhere.

cards.text: They set a day, many people come to where Paul's staying, and he teaches from morning to evening about the kingdom of God and about Jesus. Morning to EVENING, and I can't go ten minutes without checking my oven.

cards.question: To persuade the people about Jesus, what does Paul teach from?

answers.text: The Law of Moses and the Prophets
Letters from the church in Judea

cards.question: After a whole day of Paul's teaching, how do the people respond?

answers.text: Some are convinced and others refuse
Every one of them believes him
None of them will listen at all

cards.text: They disagree among themselves and start to leave. Before they go, Paul says the Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to their fathers through Isaiah the prophet (Isaiah 6:9-10).
Here are those words: "You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving."

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, why does this people hear and see but never understand?

answers.text: Nobody ever told them the message
Their teachers kept it from them

cards.question: Isaiah's words say that if this people would see, hear, understand and turn, they would be healed.

cards.text: Then comes Paul's final statement, and it's a BIG one. He tells them where God's salvation has been sent.

cards.question: Where does Paul say God's salvation has been sent?

cards.text: Paul stays two full years in his own rented house. I spent years in a junk drawer rent free, and trust me, friend, that is NOT the same thing.

cards.question: In his rented house in Rome, who does Paul welcome?

answers.text: All who come to visit him
Only the leaders of the Jews

cards.question: During those two years, Paul keeps quiet about Jesus to stay out of trouble.

cards.text: Here's how it ends: "Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ." The man's wearing a chain, and NOTHING could chain up that message.
